_comment: Council terms in one place: the public page /how-council-works renders it, the web app's timeline stage lines come from each term's `stages`, and the AI clients turn `in_the_record` (how Langford's minutes phrase it) and `we_write` (the plain words this site uses) into prompt blocks (apps/web/app/services/ai/glossary-prompt.ts, pipeline/ai/glossary.py). Public text follows docs/writing-style.md. Bump version when a `we_write` or `stages` line changes so stages that write summaries can be rerun with --stale. A term's `match` is a case-insensitive regex for the word forms pages show; the first match on a page gets a dashed underline, a hover definition and a link (components/term.tsx).

groups.title: Kinds of meetings
groups.intro: Langford Council meets in public, usually twice a month. Different kinds of meetings can do different things.

terms.means: Council's scheduled meeting, usually the first and third Monday of the month, where it makes decisions. Anyone can attend or watch the video.
terms.in_the_record: "Council Meeting", "Council Minutes".

terms.means: A meeting called outside the regular schedule, on at least a day's notice. Langford holds many, often in the afternoon before a regular meeting, for one or two items.
terms.in_the_record: "Special Council Meeting", "SP Council Minutes".

terms.means: All of Council sitting as a committee to talk things through less formally. It can only recommend. Council decides at a later meeting.
terms.in_the_record: "Committee of the Whole", "COTW". Its motions read "THAT Committee of the Whole recommend that Council…". Langford uses it mainly for budget sessions.
terms.we_write: "The committee recommended…", never "approved". A committee's vote is not the decision.

terms.means: A group of resident volunteers and staff that advises Council on one area. Langford has a Sustainable Development Advisory Committee and a Community Advisory Committee, plus a Board of Variance that decides small zoning exceptions. Committees recommend; Council decides.
terms.in_the_record: "Sustainable Development Advisory Committee", "Community Advisory Committee". Their advice reaches Council as "Committee Resolutions" or "Community Advisory Committee Meeting Resolutions – <date>".
terms.we_write: "Recommended" for what a committee did. Name the committee only when it matters.

terms.means: A meeting where residents can speak or write to Council about a proposed zoning or community plan change before Council decides. It comes after first reading and before third reading, and once it closes Council can't take new input on that proposal. Since 2023, provincial law bars a hearing for housing that already fits the community plan, and Council can waive one in other cases, so many rezonings now have none.
terms.in_the_record: "PUBLIC HEARING", usually called to order just before the Council meeting the same evening, with "PUBLIC INPUT" then "Mayor closed the Public Hearing at 7:19 pm". When none is held: "Notice of Public Hearing Being Waived".
terms.we_write: "Residents could speak or write to Council about…". Say how many spoke and what they said, when the record has it. When no hearing was held, say so plainly rather than implying one.

stages.public_hearing: Residents could speak or write to council about the proposal.

terms.means: Part of a meeting the public can't attend. Provincial law lists the only allowed reasons, such as buying or selling land, legal advice, labour talks or personnel. Council must say which reason applies, and decisions made in a closed meeting are reported later.
terms.in_the_record: "THAT Council close the meeting to the public pursuant to section 90 (1) (e) of the Community Charter to consider…", "In-camera", then "RISE AND REPORT" when it reopens.
terms.we_write: "Closed meeting". Give the reason in plain words ("about buying land"), not the section number.

terms.means: When a closed meeting ends, Council returns to open session and reports any decisions it is allowed to make public.
terms.in_the_record: "RISE AND REPORT" as an agenda heading after the closed part.
terms.we_write: "After the closed meeting, Council reported that…".

terms.means: Routine items bundled into one vote with no discussion. Any member can pull an item out to discuss it on its own.
terms.we_write: Leave consent-agenda housekeeping out of summaries unless an item was pulled and debated.
terms.in_the_record: "CONSENT AGENDA", "THAT Council adopt the recommendations for each item of the Consent Agenda as presented", with "(RECEIVE)" or "(ADOPT)" per item.

terms.means: Time set aside for residents to speak to Council. A delegation books ahead in writing and gets five minutes on any subject. Public participation is open to anyone present, three minutes each on items on that night's agenda, with no new input on a proposal that already had its public hearing.
terms.in_the_record: "DELEGATIONS", "PUBLIC PARTICIPATION". Speakers are logged as "M. Wignall, Langford Resident – re: item 5.1 – The speaker expressed support for…".
terms.we_write: "Spoke to Council", "asked Council to…". Name speakers only as the minutes name them.

terms.means: The agenda is the plan for a meeting, published beforehand. The minutes are the official written record of what was decided, approved at a later meeting. Minutes record decisions and votes, not everything that was said.
terms.we_write: Something on the agenda is not a decision. Say what happened, not what was listed.

groups.title: How Council decides
groups.intro: Every decision is a motion that members vote on. The minutes record the motion's wording and whether it passed.

terms.means: A proposal that Council votes on. One member "moves" it and another "seconds" it before it can be discussed. Every decision starts as a motion.
terms.in_the_record: "MOVED BY: MORLEY", "SECONDED: WAGNER", then "THAT Council…". Surnames only, no titles.
terms.we_write: "Decision" once it has been voted on, "proposal" before. Not "motion" in a headline.

terms.means: A decision Council makes with a single vote, without a bylaw. Most decisions, such as contracts, grants and directions to staff, are resolutions.
terms.we_write: "Council decided", "approved", "asked staff to".

terms.means: The motion passed. When no one is listed as opposed, everyone present voted yes.
terms.in_the_record: "Motion CARRIED." Recent minutes don't write "carried unanimously"; a passed motion with no "OPPOSED:" line was unanimous.
terms.we_write: "Passed" or "approved", with the count when the vote was split: "passed 6–1".

terms.means: The motion failed.
terms.in_the_record: "Motion DEFEATED."
terms.we_write: "Rejected", "voted down".

terms.means: Minutes name only the members who voted against, after the result. When no one is named, everyone present voted yes: a member who stays silent counts as a yes, and a tie means the motion is defeated. Minutes don't list who voted yes, so vote counts on this site come from attendance and the named no votes.
terms.in_the_record: "OPPOSED: Councillors Guiry, Szpak, Yacucha, and Harder." or "OPPOSED: Mayor Goodmanson" under the result line. Older minutes: "(Voting against: …)".
terms.we_write: "Passed 5–2, with X and Y opposed". Never guess who voted yes.

terms.means: A change to a motion before the vote. The amendment is voted on first, then the motion as changed.
terms.we_write: Say what the change did ("cut the fee to $200"), not "the amendment carried".
terms.in_the_record: "Amendment on the Main Motion:", its own moved, seconded and result lines, then "On the Main Motion as amended:".

terms.means: Sent to staff or a committee for more work before Council decides.
terms.in_the_record: "THAT Council refer this item to staff…".
terms.we_write: "Sent back to staff", "asked staff to report back".

terms.means: In Langford's older minutes, to "table" an item was to put it off. In much of Canada "tabled" means the opposite, presented. The word reads both ways, so this site avoids it. Recent minutes say "postpone" or "refer" instead.
terms.in_the_record: "THAT the item be tabled" in older minutes; "postpone" in recent ones. Residents speaking at hearings still say "table".
terms.we_write: "Postponed to May 9", or "set aside" when no date is given. "Presented" for an item brought before Council. Never "tabled".

terms.means: A member announces a motion they will bring to a future meeting. Nothing is decided yet.
terms.we_write: "Gave notice that they will propose…". Never count it as a decision.
terms.in_the_record: "Councillor Harder introduced the following Notice of Motion:", then moved at the next regular meeting under "NOTICE OF MOTION".

terms.means: Council cancels an earlier decision. The record rarely says why.
terms.in_the_record: "THAT Council rescind first, second and third readings of Bylaw No. 2121…", or an agenda label like "(RESCIND FIRST THREE READINGS AND GIVE NEW FIRST THREE READINGS AS AMENDED)".
terms.we_write: "Cancelled its earlier decision to…". Don't guess the reason.

stages.rescinded_reading: Council cancelled an earlier reading of the bylaw.
stages.rescinded_adoption: Council cancelled the bylaw's adoption and its readings.

terms.means: The mover took the motion back before a vote, or no one seconded it so it was never voted on.
terms.in_the_record: "The motion was withdrawn.", "received permission of the seconder and withdrew the motion", "The motion died on the floor for want of a seconder."
terms.we_write: "Withdrew the proposal". Not a vote: no count.

terms.means: A written report from City staff explaining an issue and recommending what Council should do. Council often adopts the recommendation word for word.
terms.we_write: "Staff recommended…". The report is the best source for what a decision actually does.

terms.means: A member who could gain from a decision must say so and leave the room. They don't vote on it.
terms.in_the_record: "Councillor Harder declared a perceived conflict of interest … and left the meeting at 9:51 pm".
terms.we_write: "Left the room for the vote".

terms.means: Recommendations from an advisory committee, brought to Council as a batch. Council votes on whether to act on them.
terms.in_the_record: "COMMITTEE RESOLUTIONS", "Community Advisory Committee Meeting Resolutions – January 27, 2026".
terms.we_write: "On the committee's advice, Council…".

groups.title: How a bylaw becomes law
groups.intro: A bylaw is a city law. It is voted on several times before it takes effect. Each vote is a "reading". The site explains each step in plain words instead of naming it.

terms.means: A city law. Zoning, fees, noise, parking and the budget are all bylaws. Each has a number and goes through readings before it is adopted.
terms.in_the_record: "BYLAW NO. 2220", with a long formal title such as "City of Langford Housing Agreement (777 Station Avenue) Bylaw No. 2220, 2025".
terms.we_write: Say what it does. Keep the number out of headlines and summaries: "new garbage fees", not "Bylaw 2284".

terms.means: Council votes on a bylaw several times. Each vote is a reading. BC bylaws need three readings and then adoption. Langford usually gives all three readings at one meeting and adopts the bylaw at a later one.
terms.in_the_record: Agenda labels: "(FIRST, SECOND AND THIRD READINGS)", "(SECOND AND THIRD READINGS)", "(FIRST READING)", "(ADOPTION)".
terms.we_write: Explain the step instead of naming it: "introduced", "one step from final approval", "made final".

terms.means: The bylaw is introduced. Council agrees to consider it. On its own, first reading is mostly used for community plan changes; most bylaws get all three readings at once.
terms.we_write: "Introduced", "took the first step toward…".

stages.first: Introduced to council. A bylaw needs several readings before it becomes law.

terms.means: Council approves the bylaw in principle. Usually given with first and third reading in one vote.
terms.we_write: "Approved in principle".

stages.second: Council approved the bylaw's content in principle.

terms.means: Council approves the final wording. Only adoption remains, usually at a later meeting.
terms.we_write: "One step from final approval". Don't add "a later vote is still needed": the phrase already says it.

stages.third: Council approved the final wording. Adoption is the last step.
stages.second_third: Council approved the content and final wording. Adoption is the last step.

terms.means: The final vote. The bylaw becomes law. In the minutes, "adopted" means this last step and nothing else. Zoning and community plan bylaws can be adopted the same night as third reading; others wait for a later meeting.
terms.in_the_record: "(ADOPTION)", "That Bylaw No. 2284 be adopted".
terms.we_write: "Made final", "final approval". Never "adopted" for an earlier reading, and never "adopted" for a plain resolution: that is "passed".

groups.title: Land and building
groups.intro: Most of what Council decides is about land: what can be built where, and on what conditions.

terms.means: Changing what a property may be used for, or how big a building may be. It needs a bylaw with readings and adoption, usually conditions, and sometimes a public hearing.
terms.in_the_record: "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 740 (2609 Sooke Road), Bylaw No. 2211, 2026"; file numbers like "Z25-0008".
terms.we_write: "Rezoning of 2609 Sooke Road for 47 homes". Keep file numbers out.

terms.means: Langford's long-term plan for where homes, shops and parks go. A project that doesn't fit needs a plan amendment, which is itself a bylaw.
terms.in_the_record: "OCP", "Official Community Plan Amendment".
terms.we_write: "Community plan". Spell it out; never "OCP".

terms.means: Approval of how a building looks and sits on its lot, in areas the community plan covers. Not a zoning change.
terms.in_the_record: "DP", "Development Permit".
terms.we_write: "Approved the design of…". Never "DP".

terms.means: Permission to break one specific zoning rule, such as a setback or height, for one property. Neighbours get notice and Council decides.
terms.in_the_record: "DVP24-0012", "varied pursuant to section 498". Decided under the agenda heading "NOTICE OF INTENT" after neighbours are notified; small variances can be decided by staff or the Board of Variance.
terms.we_write: "Variance", "allowed a taller building than the rules permit". Never "DVP".

terms.means: The agenda heading under which Council decides variance and temporary use permits. Neighbours are notified first and can write or speak before the vote.
terms.in_the_record: "NOTICE OF INTENT", then the permit number.
terms.we_write: Name the permit and the property, not the heading.

terms.means: Permission to use a property for something zoning doesn't allow, for up to three years, renewable once.
terms.in_the_record: "TUP21-0006", "renewed … for a period of three years". Decided under "NOTICE OF INTENT".
terms.we_write: "Temporary permit". Never "TUP".

terms.means: A contract between the City and a developer setting rents or who can live in certain homes, usually in exchange for a rezoning. It is adopted as a bylaw, so it goes through readings and adoption.
terms.we_write: "A deal to keep rents at…", with the numbers.
terms.in_the_record: "Housing Agreement (777 Station Avenue) Bylaw No. 2220".

terms.means: A promise registered on a property's title that binds future owners, such as to keep a tree or build a path.
terms.in_the_record: "Section 219 covenant".
terms.we_write: "A condition on the land". Keep "section 219" out.

terms.means: Fees developers pay toward the roads, parks, water and sewer that growth needs.
terms.in_the_record: "DCC", "Development Cost Charge Bylaw".
terms.we_write: "Developer fees for parks and roads". Never "DCC".

terms.means: A set fee developers pay per new home or lot toward amenities such as parks, recreation and daycare. Langford set it by bylaw in June 2026. Before that, contributions were negotiated deal by deal in exchange for extra density.
terms.in_the_record: "Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw No. 2275". Older minutes: "contribution … as a bonus for increased density … towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund".
terms.we_write: "The developer will pay $X toward parks and recreation". For older deals, "in exchange for extra density".

terms.means: Dividing one lot into several. Mostly decided by staff. Council sees it when a bylaw or road is involved.
terms.we_write: "Split into three lots".

terms.means: Langford's five-year budget, adopted each spring as a bylaw before the tax rates. The first year is this year's budget.
terms.in_the_record: "2026–2030 Financial Plan Bylaw No. 2281".
terms.we_write: "The 2026 budget".

terms.means: Sets this year's property tax rates. Adopted with the budget, by May 15.
terms.we_write: "Property taxes", with the change for a typical home when the record gives it.
terms.in_the_record: "Tax Rates Bylaw No. 2282, 2026".

terms.means: A flat charge on each property in an area for one service, such as sewer, on top of regular property tax.
terms.we_write: "A $X-a-year charge on homes in…".

terms.means: Chairs Council meetings and votes like other members. Elected city-wide every four years.
terms.we_write: "Mayor" and their name as the record gives it. Never guess pronouns.

terms.means: One of six elected members besides the mayor. Each has one vote.
terms.we_write: "Councillor" and their name. Don't assume someone's title: check the roster for the meeting date.

terms.means: City employees, led by the Chief Administrative Officer. They write reports, recommend, and carry out decisions. They don't vote.
terms.in_the_record: "Director of Community Planning & Climate Change", "Director of Development Services", "Corporate Officer", "CAO".
terms.we_write: "Staff", or the role in plain words ("the City's planning director").

terms.means: Whoever runs a meeting. Usually the mayor; an acting mayor takes over when the mayor is away, on a rotation set each year.
A panel of appointed residents, separate from Council, that can allow small exceptions to zoning rules where following them would cause hardship.
terms.we_write: "The Board of Variance allowed…"; never "Council".
